__comment: Canonical content spine for jakeruth.com rebuild. Every experience reads from this. DO NOT invent facts outside this file. If a needed fact isn't here, use a tasteful placeholder and note it.

identity.status_line: Re-entering the workforce. Running Stock Unlock has been on autopilot for ~15 months. Open to full-time roles, contract work, or equity-founding conversations.

pitches: Thirteen years shipping. One chapter ending, another beginning.
Engineer. Founder. Occasional unicyclist on Rubik's cubes.
Built a company. Wound it down to profit. Shopping for what's next.
Shipped more than I'm allowed to say, at companies you've heard of.
why_me: Founded and ran a profitable SaaS without burning venture dollars. That perspective doesn't come from a bootcamp.
I've been the senior IC who knows the codebase cold AND the CEO who raised a seed. Those two rarely live in the same person.
Ships production code on day one. No onboarding curve — just let me loose.

timeline.detail: Soccer + track captain. Unmotivated academically except math/science — 88-89 average. Accelerated math track since 3rd grade.
Took the class specifically to dodge AP Calculus. Fell in love with code in the first week.
BS Computer Science + Applied Mathematics, 3.88 GPA. Dean's List every semester.
Took over a failing club. Recruited 20+ members. Organized the field trip to Tekkapalooza where he handed out his resume to CommerceHub.
Part-time through senior year of college, full-time after. Learned real engineering: code reviews, micro-service architecture, test discipline.
3.88 GPA, dual major in CS + Applied Math.
College social media iOS app on React Native v0.13. Thousands of signups across two campuses. Couldn't solve cold-start. Shut down within ~6 months.
Interviewed at Google twice (final rounds, never offered). Landed at Oscar Health.
Joined at ~50 engineers under Alan Warren (formerly scaled Google Docs from 2-3 to thousands). Left at ~150+. Leveled Associate → Mid → Senior. Declined manager track.
Built a Python script to automate Daniel's weekend spreadsheet work. Emailed Daniel weekly, got ignored. Daniel eventually replied. First call was a video call with a beer.

timeline.event: Left Oscar to co-found Stock Unlock
timeline.detail: Brought Nick Puljik (ex-Oscar). YC reached out cold via LinkedIn before they even applied.
$500K YC SAFE + $835K from other investors. Jake was CEO, led the YC interview.
YC pushed them to launch before raising. 400 paying users in two weeks. 800-900 at seed close.
Grew to thousands of paying customers, 8 employees at peak. Hit a stall point late 2024.
Company continues with three full-time employees. Jake moved to key-decisions-only. Focus: operate profitably, not grow at all costs.

Opus 4.5 was the tipping point. Rewrote SU marketing in Webflow, overhauled SEO/GEO, migrated off Customer.io to AWS SES (saved $6K/yr), built a tightly-permissioned internal Discord bot for log/error/code/user-data queries.

values.core_conviction: Overcharging for bad software is theft from people who can't afford to be robbed.
anti_patterns: 'Fisher-Price' software that looks polished but breaks under real use
Post-IPO culture decay — lowered hiring bar, benefit cuts
Overcharging retail investors for broken analysis tools
wants: Brutally honest teammates who disagree directly, with reason
Things that matter, that aren't bullshit

ai_philosophy.one_line: Driver in the driver's seat, not driven by the car.
ai_philosophy.longer: There's a real distinction between vibe coding and software engineering. Human-reviewed for business logic, security, and system architecture. AI-only acceptable for static front-end visualization. Opus 4.5 was the inflection point. Currently heavy on Claude Code + Codex + CMUX.

values.concrete_bad_example: A competitor's 'margin of safety score' computed as (current_price / all_time_high). Jake called this 'ape-shit retarded.' Stock Unlock exists partly as a response.

hire_options.framing_rule: DO NOT list specific dollar prices. Use 'Contact', 'Talk to Jake', 'Let's talk', 'Market rate + equity'. Pricing UI is fine; real numbers are not.

stories.title: The AP CS switch
stories.detail: Senior year of high school, Jake needed a math credit but refused to take AP Calculus. Ms. Nalbandian mentioned she taught AP Computer Science. Jake asked if it counted as a math credit. She said yes. He took it to avoid Calc. Fell in love with coding in the first week. That sideways pivot became his career.

stories.title: The production takedown
stories.detail: As a CommerceHub intern, Jake took down production with one button press. Apologized before anyone spoke in the meeting. Manager stood up: 'that wasn't your fault — you shouldn't have had access to that button.' The system was the problem, not the intern.

stories.title: The Pronk emails
stories.detail: Jake wrote a Python script in a weekend to automate Daniel's spreadsheet work. Emailed him free. Got ignored. Kept emailing. Daniel eventually replied to make him stop. Instead of going away, Jake hopped on a video call, cracked a beer, and started Stock Unlock.

stories.title: The unicycle cube
stories.detail: At an Oscar Health talent show, Jake rode a unicycle while solving a Rubik's cube. Josh Kushner was in the audience.

stories.title: The Customer.io hack-off
stories.detail: In 2026, Jake migrated Stock Unlock off Customer.io by self-hosting on AWS SES with custom admin panels, built largely with AI. Saved $5-6K/yr. One person, one weekend of focused work.

contact.response_posture: Fast during business hours ET. Prefers email to DMs.
